name: CO-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of about 20 points
Incumbent Joe Neguse running with a large financial advantage
Prediction markets price Neguse near 97% to win
No competitive polling or expert ratings signal any risk
model.rationale: This seat's fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Neguse: a roughly 20-point Democratic lean, incumbency, and a fundraising edge of more than $2.7 million raised against a Republican challenger with no reported finances. Markets price Neguse near 97%, consistent with a Safe Democratic rating.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a dramatically shifted national environment would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race, though even that would likely fall short in a district this blue.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Joe Neguse seeks another term in a northern Colorado district that leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about 20 points. He enters the race with more than $3 million on hand after raising over $2.7 million, while Republican Kelley Dennison reports no fundraising and Libertarian Gaylon Kent is also on the ballot.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, but prediction markets put Neguse's chances near 97 percent. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and a lopsided money advantage makes this one of the safest Democratic-held seats on the map this cycle.
